content.content: Read the dependent's ignore artifact and the packaged set the dependent commits to against the packaged set the prerequisite records, in both directions. The prerequisite's set is the runtime payload exactly — out/extension.js, media/webview.html, src/styles/*.css, src/webview/main.js, and from node_modules only @vscode/codicons/dist/codicon.css with the codicon.ttf it loads — plus the packaging metadata the packager force-includes, the manifest and the README, which the ignore artifact can neither add nor keep out. LOOSER: fail when the packaged set the dependent commits to, or the filtering its artifact produces, admits a file outside that set — a TypeScript source, test, design note, node document, schema, build configuration, or a dependency the payload does not name. STRICTER: fail when the dependent's packaged set denies a file the prerequisite names, including the manifest or the README. The check does not require README.md to exist in the repository: the manifest and the README are metadata by virtue of what the packager includes, and the dependent is judged on stating and enforcing that the runtime payload and the packaging metadata are distinct, not on the file being present. Fail naming the file and the direction it diverges in.
content.rationale: The dependent's artifact is the packaging ignore file, a tool-checkable artifact (code layer), while the packaged set is stated in prose (natural layer), so the edge sits in the matrix's natural-to-code cell and takes the fidelity form: the prose cannot itself decide, file by file, what the packager will carry, so the ignore artifact is where conformance is settled, and the artifact and the packaged set the dependent commits to must enforce the prose exactly, no stricter and no looser, with each divergence named. Fidelity is a review, not a runnable listing: the refined prerequisite adds packaging metadata the packager includes independently of the ignore artifact, and a packager listing cannot show force-included metadata that is absent from the tree, so a file-list test would fail for the file's absence rather than for the dependent's claim and would need a file this decision does not own. Reading the artifact's effect and the packaged set the dependent states against the prerequisite in both directions keeps the check independent of the dependent's wording — any rewrite that commits to the same packaged set passes — while a set that drops the manifest or README, or admits an extra file, fails naming it. The prose is unenforced until the dependent commits to and enforces the runtime/metadata distinction this check reads.
